A premature male infant, born at 35 weeks' gestation, develops acute symptoms three days after birth
including high fever, seizures, and hypotonia. The pregnancy history reveals maternal fever and
chorioamnionitis during the third trimester, with no prenatal care. The infant's Apgar scores were 6 at
both 1 and 5 minutes. Current vital signs show temperature of 39.0°C (102.2°F), pulse 124/min,
respirations 31/min, and blood pressure 81/53 mm Hg. Clinical examination reveals grunting breath
sounds, normal cardiac findings, and hepatomegaly. Cerebral ultrasound demonstrates diffuse
hyperechogenicity. What is the most likely underlying risk factor that predisposed this newborn to his
current condition? Answer Choices: (A) Exposure to contaminated water during pregnancy (B)
Maternal contact with cat feces during pregnancy (C) Postnatal transmission of cytomegalovirus (D)
Exposure to contaminated soil during pregnancy (E) Maternal consumption of raw fish during
pregnancy (F) Maternal occupational exposure to farm animals (G) Maternal consumption of
unpasteurized cheese during pregnancy (H) Maternal herpes simplex infection during delivery (I)
Contact with infected respiratory droplets after birth (J) Maternal urinary tract infection during third

trimester
 A. Exposure to contaminated water during pregnancy
B. Postnatal transmission of cytomegalovirus
C. Maternal consumption of raw fish during pregnancy
D. Maternal herpes simplex infection during delivery
E. Maternal contact with cat feces during pregnancy
